messages:
Sofia M.: quick heads-up — proposal to switch europe-west admission from full-degrade to a short-queue policy during peak windows. seen growing p95 gen latency and a few OOMs when we keep degrading. want to discuss.
James L.: can you share numbers? p95/p99 and queue lengths?
Sofia M.: p95 token latency for gen jumps from 140ms -> 420ms under degrade mode at 80% GPU util. p99 spikes to ~1.2s. queue depth currently capped by degrade so we avoid OOMs but client-facing latency is bad. we also see ~2% increase in failed websocket streams.
Li Wei: what does "short-queue" mean operationally? will it block callers longer or return 429s? how do clients retry safely?
Sofia M.: short-queue = allow small in-memory queue per worker (max_queue_ms ~3s / length 6 requests), then fall back to degrade for a small fraction (10%) for long-tail requests, and after that reject with proper Retry-After. idea is to give transient bursts a chance while bounding memory.
Alex R.: big caveat: europe-west has several pods routing to us while a neighboring region is hitting network egress limits — we've seen spikes pushing traffic into eu, that's what saturates the fleet. queueing will increase in-flight memory and may expose preemption on GCP preemptible nodes. is that acceptable?
Priya K.: from cost POV: queueing doesn't consume extra GPU cycles vs degrade (degrade still runs smaller models or shorter outputs). but queueing increases latency which could increase token consumption if clients retry naively. need to ensure we return 429 + Retry-After for rejects to avoid thundering herd.
infra-bot: metric snapshot: queue_depth: 54 -> 180 in last 15m; gpu_util_avg: 82%; preemptions_last_hour: 4; websocket_errors: +1.8% (see dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/eu/queue)
James L.: can we do canary on a slice of traffic? maybe 10% of requests routed to short-queue policy for 2 hours during the next peak window.
Sofia M.: yes. propose canary wednesday 06:00-08:00 UTC at 10% traffic. rollback triggers: >5% increase in client timeouts, >1.5x p99 latency, or >2 preemptions.
Li Wei: add client-side guidance in the SDK: treat 429 as retryable with exponential backoff + jitter, but cap retries to 2 within 30s. also add a warning that function-call websockets should prefer streaming early tokens to avoid large buffers.
Alex R.: config draft (for rollout):
```
{
  "admission_policy": "short_queue",
  "max_queue_ms": 3000,
  "max_queue_len": 6,
  "degrade_fraction": 0.10,
  "reject_after_ms": 5000,
  "retry_header": "Retry-After"
}
```
Priya K.: need to set rate-limit windows per customer too — high-tier customers should get larger queue caps or can bypass to degrade-first. will update pricing impacts after canary.
James L.: how do we surface this in console? ops runbook needs steps: enable policy, monitor p99/p95, rollback, contact owners. also add a checkbox for 'allow short-queue in region'.
Sofia M.: owners: @Sofia M., @James L., @Li Wei. infra to run canary and monitor. ops: Priya to assess cost delta after run. infra-bot please create canary runbook reminder and tag the alerts.
infra-bot: created runbook: /playbooks/admit-shortqueue-eu and scheduled reminder for 2024-08-14T06:00:00Z. alert channel #eng-oncall.
Priya K.: ack — i'll check cost projections and update tomorrow.
James L.: ack. i'll add SDK retry guidance PR and console toggle change.
Sofia M.: thanks everyone. running canary next wed 06:00 UTC. will follow up with results + dashboards. :thumbsup:
thread_text: proposal to switch europe-west admission from full-degrade to a short-queue policy during peak windows; canary scheduled; owners assigned
